newsitem.title: FRANCE: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE SCORE HARD-FOUGHT WIN OVER WALES.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-FRANCE SCORE HARD-FOUGHT WIN OVER WALES.

text.p: France stayed on course for the Five Nations title with a hard-fought 27-22 win over Wales at Parc des Princes on Saturday.
France scored four tries to three in a tight contest which could have gone either way as Wales, striving for their first victory in Paris since 1975, staged a furious onslaught in the final minutes.

A try by powerful lock Olivier Merle converted by Richard Dourthe gave France a 7-0 lead after just three minutes but 13 minutes later, Wales responded with a try by winger Gareth Thomas which Neil Jenkins converted.

The visitors moved in front in the 21st minute with a Jenkins penalty but two brilliant tries by Laurent Leflamand and David Venditti followed by a penalty from David Aucagne allowed France to turn around leading 20-10.
The second half saw Wales fight back with a try by centre Alan Bateman converted by Jenkins in the 56th minute.

A vicious rebound which surprised two Welsh players then gave Leflamand his second try. Aucagne converted it and France were leading 27-17 with 15 minutes remaining, only for number eight Scott Quinnell to set up scrum-half Robert Howley for Wales' third try three minutes later.
With Jenkins missing a crucial conversion, France clung on to a five-point lead until the final whistle despite the Welsh pressure.
